anchor.note: Big-O notation, listed in the reader profile and as a known concept.
Integers modulo 2 under modular arithmetic, covered by the introductory discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic) in the reader profile.

gaps.quote: Its tape cost is what saves a power in the transform layers of the multiplication algorithm.
gaps.note: The page never gives the cost of applying the factors one at a time as a bound, nor says which multiplication algorithm is meant, so the reader cannot check that the tape cost saves a power.

gaps.term: chunk moves of a change of basis
gaps.quote: and each change of basis moves whole chunks.
gaps.note: The page asserts that a change of basis on address positions moves whole chunks but does not say how a map on address bits acts on chunks.

gaps.quote: which exchanges banks of values with prescribed signs
gaps.note: The page says the network computes the layer's chunk moves but does not explain how its banked, signed exchanges realise those moves for this layer.

gaps.quote: Splitting complete rows among the network's wire roles gives each recursive call a fixed fraction, below one, of the volume, and each level cuts the active chunks by a fixed factor.
gaps.note: "Complete rows" and "wire roles" are not defined, and the fraction and factor are not given or derived, so the reader cannot check the recursion's shrinkage.

gaps.quote: The levels sum to $O(d^{\lambda'})$ per stored bit
gaps.note: The summation is presented as following from the recursion, but the level bounds it depends on are not stated on the page; the reader can only defer to the source.
